newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index edges up to 326.32.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index edges up to 326.32.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, was slightly higher at 326.32 the start of play on Thursday.
Latin America rose to 621.33 from 620.58, Asia was down at 263.28 from 263.36 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were down to 157.69 from 157.80.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high this year of 315.20 after the close of play on January 27.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars BFFO, was down 0.20 percent day-on-day at 176.15 at 0950 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high of 171.22 after the end of trading on January 20.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD was down 0.17 percent at 524.52, calculated after the close of trade on Tuesday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. Its 1997 high of 508.674 was also reached on January 20.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 30 emerging market countries after adding Russia, Slovakia, Egypt and Morocco on February 3. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.06 percent to 127.70 by the start of trade on Thursday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996, and reached a 1997 high of 125.93 after the close of trade on 16 January.
By region, Latin America was up 0.55 percent at 106.53, Asia fell 0.05 to 133.89 and East Europe was down 0.27 at 159.68.
